title: Sandpile Avalanche Cellular Automaton
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with an interactive 3D sandpile avalanche cellular automaton (Abelian Sandpile Model) using Three.js.

SCENE SETUP:
- Use an orthographic camera looking down at a grid from above at a slight angle (position: 0, 40, 25; lookAt: 0, 0, 0).
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.4) and a directional light from (10, 30, 10) with intensity 0.8.
- The grid is NxN where N=31 (odd, so there is a center cell). Each cell is represented by a 3D box (BoxGeometry 0.9x0.9x0.9) placed on an invisible plane.
- The height (y-position) of each box equals its grain count * 0.5. Color each cell based on grain count: 0=dark gray (#333333), 1=green (#22aa22), 2=yellow (#dddd00), 3=orange (#ff8800), 4+=red (#ff0000).
- Background color: #1a1a2e.

CELLULAR AUTOMATON RULES (Abelian Sandpile):
- Each cell holds an integer number of grains >= 0.
- A cell is unstable if grains >= 4.
- When a cell topples: it loses 4 grains, and each of its 4 orthogonal neighbors gains 1 grain.
- Grains that fall off the grid edge are lost (open boundary).
- One full simulation step processes ALL currently unstable cells simultaneously (parallel toppling), then updates the grid. This is one 'avalanche step'.
- An 'avalanche' is the sequence of steps from adding a grain until the grid is fully stable (all cells < 4).

USER INTERACTIONS:
1. CLICK on the 3D grid (raycasting) to drop 1 grain on the clicked cell. This triggers a full avalanche (all steps until stable) animated step-by-step at the current speed.
2. Press SPACE to drop 1 grain on the CENTER cell (15,15) and trigger avalanche.
3. Press 'R' to reset the entire grid to all zeros.
4. Press 'F' to fill every cell with exactly 3 grains (critical state) — next drop causes massive avalanche.
5. Press '+' or '=' to increase simulation speed (fewer ms per step: cycle through 500, 200, 100, 50, 20, 5 ms).
6. Press '-' to decrease simulation speed (more ms per step, reverse cycle).
7. Press 'P' to pause/resume an ongoing avalanche.

During an avalanche, user clicks and SPACE are ignored (no new grains while avalanche is running, unless paused then still ignored).

STATE MANAGEMENT — expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- gridSize: 31 (constant)
- grid: a flat Int32Array of length 31*31 representing current grain counts (row-major: index = row*31+col)
- totalGrains: total number of grains currently on the grid (sum of all cells)
- totalDropped: cumulative grains dropped by user since last reset
- totalLostToBoundary: cumulative grains lost off edges since last reset
- avalancheActive: boolean, true if avalanche is currently running
- avalancheSteps: number of toppling steps in the current/last avalanche
- avalancheTopplings: total number of individual cell topplings in the current/last avalanche
- paused: boolean
- speedMs: current ms per avalanche step
- maxGrains: the maximum grain count on any single cell right now
- unstableCells: number of cells with grains >= 4 right now
- lastDropCell: {row, col} of the last cell where a grain was dropped, or null
- stepsSinceReset: total avalanche steps executed since last reset

CONSERVATION LAW: At all times, totalGrains + totalLostToBoundary === totalDropped. Enforce and track this.

HUD (DOM overlay, top-left):
- Display: Total Grains, Grains Dropped, Grains Lost, Avalanche Steps, Topplings, Speed (ms), Paused status, Unstable Cells.
- Style: semi-transparent dark background, white monospace text, 14px font.
- Include a small instruction line at the bottom: 'Click/Space=drop | R=reset | F=fill | +/-=speed | P=pause'

ENSURE:
- All 3D box heights and colors update each avalanche step.
- The simulation is visually smooth and each step is visible.
- Grid is centered at world origin.
- No errors on boundary cells (edge grains are simply lost).
- The __3D_STATE__ object is updated BEFORE each render frame and AFTER each avalanche step.
physics_constraints: Abelian sandpile conservation: totalGrains + totalLostToBoundary === totalDropped at all times. Each topple removes exactly 4 grains from a cell and distributes 1 to each orthogonal neighbor (lost if off-grid). Parallel toppling: all unstable cells topple simultaneously per step. Grains are non-negative integers. Stable state means all cells < 4.
